description: The judgements of the solver as data. A kind is one function of editor/solver.js; a record is one judgement with its id, and a line of a kit it made carries that id, so a wrong line points at its judgement or at the engine.

judgements.says: {0} on the pins of its IO MUX
judgements.why: A host on the pins of its own IO MUX runs at its full speed, and wired boards often take them: SPI3 of the terminal and of dotview-clock is on 23 and 18. Taken only when every line of the host is free there; a pin the solver keeps out, as a strapping pin, leaves the host to other pins, so SPI2 of an ESP32, whose MISO is GPIO 12, is not on its IO MUX in a kit while the terminal has it there.

judgements.says: {0} is a strapping pin ({1}): nothing on it should hold a level of its own at reset
judgements.says_unless: {0} is a strapping pin ({1}): {2} holds no level on it at reset, so the kit takes it
judgements.why: A strapping pin is sampled at reset. The datasheet gives what it selects and the rows of the table of boot modes (gpio.boot_modes, gpio.pins.*.boot of the chip); the solver reads from them the harm of a level there: run, where the start of the program or the voltage of the flash depends on it, download, where only a download mode does, none otherwise. The kit keeps out the harms listed here and a strapping pin the datasheet does not describe; it may take the others, as GPIO 5 of an ESP32, which the terminal takes for a CS. The lines of a part whose logic is none, which holds nothing on them, may have any of them all the same: a pin sampled at reset is harmed by a line that pulls it, and such a line pulls nowhere. The kit gives them those pins last, when the free ones run out: a free pin asks nothing of reset, such a pin is often a pin of JTAG too, which is a cost, and a kit that fits without them stays as it was. Only the lines of a way have them, which no other part shares.

judgements.says: {0} is a pin of JTAG: the kit leaves no debugging by JTAG on it
judgements.why: A note of the docs of ESP-IDF on a pin keeps it out of a kit. The pins of JTAG are a cost, not a danger: a kit may take them, and says so, as the terminal and dotview-clock take 13 and 14 of an ESP32 for SPI2.

judgements.says: {0}: the board has one, of a variant the data does not name, and a module of the catalog names it
judgements.why: A part of a board whose data names no variant may or may not be the variant asked: counted as an answer with an unknown, it came before a kit with a module that names the variant (an imported AtomS3R with some LED before a DevKit with a 7-segment backpack). Where the catalog has a module that names the variant, the part of the board answers nothing and stays a line; where none does, it stays an answer with the unknown, as before.

judgements.says: LEDC: {0} channels asked, the chip has {1}
judgements.why: A way of a part names the LEDC channels it takes (ledc of the way: the OE of a chain of shift registers, the three colours of an RGB LED). They and the outputs of the page come out of the same channels of the chip (frequency_sources.ledc.outputs): a kit that asks more is refused, before its pins are counted.

judgements.says: {0}: it takes {1} V as high by its datasheet, and {2} V drove it on hardware: a level shifter on its line is the sure way
judgements.why: A datasheet gives the least high an input takes, and a chip of 3.3 V gives less than some ask: the WS2812B takes 0.7 VDD, 3.5 V at 5 V. Where a trial on hardware drove it with less (high_seen_mv of the chip, with its checked entry), the kit says so and adds no level shifter: a garland of 360 WS2812B runs from a GPIO of an ESP32. A chip with no such trial gets the shifter, and a margin nobody measured is not assumed.

judgements.says: {0}: its lines go up to {1} V and the pins of this chip take {2} V by its datasheet; on hardware they ran together with no level shifter: a level shifter on them is the sure way
judgements.why: The pins of a chip of 3.3 V take a little more than 3.3 V by its datasheet, and a module whose pull-ups go to 5 V puts 5 V on them through those pull-ups. Where a trial on hardware ran such a module straight on the pins (logic_seen_mv of its device, with its checked entry), the kit says so and adds no level shifter, as for a level seen on a WS2812B. A module with no such trial gets the shifter.
